plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all leveraged ETF exposure, aligning with capital preservation.
Trim SPY to 20% and CRWD to 10% to reduce concentration and meet the single name mandate.

conservative.read: This conservative plan targets a potential ~1.5% monthly return, prioritizing capital preservation. It significantly reduces risk by eliminating leveraged ETFs and lowering concentration, but still carries market exposure.

plan: Trim SOXL to 3% and SPAL to 2% to reduce leveraged ETF exposure while maintaining a small allocation.
Reduce SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Buy ALB at 4% to introduce a new, high-quality name from the scanner.
Add to CRWD, increasing its allocation to 16%, leveraging its strong performance.
balanced.read: This balanced plan aims for a ~2.5% monthly return, focusing on risk-first growth. It reduces overall leverage and concentration while blending broad market exposure with quality tech and a small amount of leveraged exposure.

plan: Trim SPY to 25% to meet the single name concentration mandate.
Add to SOXL and SPAL, increasing each to 6%, to lean into leveraged ETFs for aggressive growth.
Buy ALB at 6% to add a high-scoring scanner setup.
Increase CRWD to 16% and SMH to 15% to concentrate in strong-performing tech and semiconductor sectors.
aggressive.read: This aggressive plan targets a ~4% monthly return, stretching for growth. It significantly increases exposure to leveraged ETFs and concentrates in high-scoring setups, which amplifies both potential upside and drawdown. Daily decay and rebalancing of leveraged ETFs mean strict stop discipline is crucial to manage rapid losses.

plan: Sell SOXL and SPAL to zero to eliminate all high-beta leveraged exposure.
Add to QQQI, increasing its allocation to 30%, to prioritize income and covered-call strategies.
Trim SPY to 20% to reduce concentration and balance the portfolio.
Reduce CRWD to 5% and SMH to 5% to minimize exposure to high-beta single names and sectors.
income.read: This income plan targets a ~1% monthly return, focusing on parking cash for yield. It prioritizes low drawdown and reliable income by rotating into income/covered-call ETFs and broad index funds, while cutting high-beta names. Distributions are variable, and NAV can still fall in selloffs.
